Braided currents with dark channels and caustic lines carried at the water's own speed, a warm halo, glints, a soft edge, weaving in the gutter clear of the text.
The stream crosses from one gutter to the other in the clear space above the text and runs down beside it, flowing, with no kink at the bends.
Water runs the bar, clings round the end and lets go; the falling front gains ground faster each frame and the stream thins and tears as it speeds up.
The stream arrives, a crown of fingers and thrown drops on arcs burst at impact, then a sheet spreads along the top edge and the impact keeps churning while water arrives.
After the landing burst the sheet runs along the plate's top edge with a bright bead at its leading edge.
The sheet gathers at the corner, clings a little round it and pours off along its tangent into a fall that speeds up.
A strong impact at the bar's centre, drops thrown both ways, then the water divides and runs both ways along the top.
Both halves pour off the bar's ends and fall down either side of the placards, framing the section.
The stream reaches the pool and the pool spreads from the inflow over a second and a half, with a meniscus, rings and a small splash at the inflow.
The plate's side toward the stream glows warm amber, strongest on the bevel facing it, falling off across the plate, words still readable.
Braided currents with dark channels and caustic lines carried at the water's own speed, a warm halo, glints, a soft edge, weaving in the gutter clear of the text.

The ribbon is an even-width glowing tube from the top bar down the right side, with no sparks, no halo, no bright head and no dry channel ahead of it, so it is plainly less alive than the reference with its particles and halo, and the faint "the body" label sits on top of the "Brandon Church" wordmark at top left.

Across all eight frames the head is a blunt bright stub that creeps down the left edge, with nothing thrown ahead of it and no particles riding the flow, and it runs through empty space instead of over a surface, so there is no thin sheet, leading edge, travelling ripple or lip bead to read as a run.

The stream pouring off the right end of the plate stays one hair-thin, even line from 0.27 s to 0.63 s and never thins or breaks into strands or drops, no particles ride it, and the incoming fall at top left runs straight down through the "Brandon Church" wordmark in every frame.

The impact on the top right corner from 0.64 s to 0.99 s throws straight streaks like a spark burst, with no crown rising and collapsing and no drops falling back on arcs, and the plate face next to the impact picks up no amber light (its warm right side at 0.30 s goes away in later frames instead of growing).

Across 1.4 s the water only lands on the top left corner and creeps right along the top edge, it never wraps round a corner and lets go, so the move this strip names is not shown, the splash is straight spark rays with no crown, and the bronze plate takes no amber light where the water touches it.

The pour over the right end does cling and let go between 0.75 s and 1.05 s, but the stream it drops is an even thin line ending in a hard bright dot with no thinning, strands or riding particles, the landing at top left is only a few straight spark rays with no crown, and the sheet on the top edge reads as a flat bright line with no leading edge or ripples.

The impact on the CLIENT WORK bar at 0.50 s is a symmetric firework of straight rays, not a crown with arcing drops, and by 1.70 s the sheet has only crept a short way each side with no pour over either end, no falls down the sides and no join beneath, so it shows less of the interaction than the reference and does not light the bar the way the reference lights its plates.
